rules.rule: An instance setup is {"__type":"Instance","rootDevice":{"<id>":<Device>}} with exactly one key under rootDevice. IDevice::loadConfiguration takes the Device object itself.
Every object carries __type. Folders are Folder (FB, Sig, IP, Dev) or IoFolder (IO and nested IO folders); a missing or wrong __type aborts the load.

A setup is a full description, not a patch: a property missing from propValues resets to its default, a missing name sets the name to an empty string, a missing active, visible or public sets it to true.

Every removable function block is removed when its parent loads; only blocks listed under FB are created again, from typeId, with ComponentConfig applied over the type's default config. The items key becomes the block's local ID.
A function block entry without typeId aborts the load; a typeId no loaded module provides is skipped with a warning.

A sub-device is matched by its Dev items key and updated in place, or added from connectionString. With both manufacturer and serialNumber present the loader runs discovery and prefers the matching device.

A newly added sub-device gets the local ID its module assigns, not the items key; signal IDs that pass through it must use the module's ID (the reference device module assigns RefDev<n> for daqref://device<n>).
Connected devices missing from Dev stay unless UpdateParameters.RemoveUnusedDevices is set.
InputPort.signalId is a global ID whose first segment is the root device's local ID (openDAQDevice by default); a different root ID drops the connection.
Channels, signals, IO folders, input ports and custom components are never created by a load; unknown local IDs are skipped. A setup can only set their attributes and property values.
Srv, the Synchronization component, tags, connectionStatuses, __version, isRootDevice, className and the input port's name and public are written by save and ignored by load.
Write DaqDeviceInfo in each device's propValues, at least {"__type":"DeviceInfo","propValues":{}}, like every object property; omitting it clears its values.

Bool, int and string are plain JSON; floats carry a decimal point; lists are arrays or {"__type":"List","values":[...]}; dicts {"__type":"Dict","values":[{"key":..,"value":..}]}; selections are the integer index; enumerations, ratios, structs, ranges and complex numbers use their tagged forms; nested objects {"__type":<serialize id>,"propValues":{...}}. Never null.
Struct and enumeration type names must be registered in the target's type manager, which happens when the module that defines them is loaded.
Property values are applied in the object's property order, not file order, through setProtectedPropertyValue, so read-only properties are written too.
A property value that fails to set aborts the whole load and leaves input ports unconnected; a failing sub-device is logged and skipped.
